$about: PHASE B — BUILD THE i18n LAYER BASE UI DOES NOT HAVE.
base-ui-i18n.json MEASURED the gap: zero locale bundles, zero strings
provider, zero locale context, eight announced English strings, seven
reachable by prop and one not. This file records what was BUILT against that
measurement, what it actually closes, and — the part that matters more — what
it does NOT close and why.
THE HEADLINE: all seven reachable strings now resolve from ONE locale, during
the server render, and a suite pins each of them. The eighth is confirmed
still unreachable at 1.7.0 from the installed dist and is drafted for
upstream. A second, unreported Base UI defect — server-rendered controls with
no accessible name — is drafted too, with a first-hand repro.
THE HONEST DEDUCTION: of the seven, only two are wired into a SHIPPED Lumo
component by this work. Three were already closed by required props that
predate the layer, and two have no Base UI-engine Lumo component to wire into
yet. That breakdown is in `coverage` and is not rounded up.
measured_from: the installed dist at node_modules/.pnpm/@base-ui+react@1.7.0_.../node_modules/@base-ui/react, plus renders executed in packages/ui's vitest config

the_gap_restated.why_a_layer_was_needed_rather_than_seven: A prop reaches the string; a prop does not stop you forgetting it. All seven are ARIA attributes — invisible in review, invisible in a screenshot, wrong only to the person listening. Base UI's own default for the slider range is the proof of how quiet the failure is: «۲۰ start range» is HALF localised, digits obeying Slider.Root's `locale` prop and words not, so a reviewer who does not read Persian sees ۲۰ and passes it.

catalogue.why_server_safe: every export is a pure function of a `Locale` value. There is no provider to be absent, no effect to not run, and no `window` to be missing.
catalogue.enforcement: `satisfies Record<Locale, BaseUiStringTemplates>` — a new locale without a string set is a compile error, and so is one missing key. Modelled on packages/core/src/strings.ts, which states the same rule for Lumo's own required strings.

two_types_not_one.BaseUiStringTemplates: the AUTHORED form. The slider entries take an already-formatted STRING.
two_types_not_one.BaseUiStrings: the CONSUMED form, returned by `baseUiStringsFor(locale)`. The slider entries take a NUMBER and an optional Intl.NumberFormatOptions.
two_types_not_one.why_the_split_is_the_enforcement: a translator authoring a locale cannot reach the raw number, because at that layer it does not exist. Reaching it would mean `${value}` — a bare JavaScript number interpolated into an ARIA attribute, in Latin digits, on a Persian page. That is LumoNode's rule-0 defect in the one place LumoNode cannot see, since aria-valuetext is not a text node. `baseUiStringsFor` is the only thing that can supply the number, and it supplies it through `formatNumber(value, locale, options)`.

catalogue.no_duplicate_persian: numberField.roleDescription is READ FROM LumoStrings rather than re-authored. One concept, one Persian phrase; a test asserts the two agree for every locale.

provider.mechanism: reads the EXISTING LumoLocaleContext and calls baseUiStringsFor. No new context, no new Provider.
provider.why_no_second_provider: there is exactly one locale lever in Lumo. A LumoStringsProvider beside LumoLocaleContext would be a SECOND lever, and two levers that can disagree is precisely the defect base-ui-i18n.json records against Base UI itself — a per-component `locale` prop and a global DirectionProvider with nothing tying them together. The strings are DERIVED from the locale, never passed alongside it, the same rule `direction()` follows.
provider.resolution_rule: a component whose frozen public API already carries a required `locale` prop (Slider, ProgressBar, Meter, ToastRegion) calls baseUiStringsFor(locale) with THAT prop. The hook is for components with no locale prop of their own (NumberField, DateField). One source per component, always.
provider.server_reach_verified: asserted under renderToStaticMarkup in every case of the suite below — never jsdom.

wiring.added: thumbValueText(locale, formatOptions, thumbCount) — a named function returning Base UI's (formattedValue, value, index) callback
wiring.honesty: Lumo ships ONE thumb, so only the thumbCount<2 branch executes in the shipped component. The range branch is not dead code for a bogus reason: Lumo components are COPIED, not imported, and a consumer adding a range slider edits THIS FILE and adds <Slider.Thumb index={1}>, at which point Base UI's half-localised default takes over. getAriaValueText is consulted before that default (SliderThumb.mjs:244), so the second thumb is correct on the first byte it is ever rendered rather than correct only if the person adding it read the comment.
wiring.why_thumbCount_and_not_index_gt_0: on a single-thumb slider index 0 must be the bare formatted number; on a range it must be «۲۰ آغاز بازه». The two cases differ at the SAME index, so the count is the only thing separating them — which is exactly what Base UI's own `values.length === 2` check does.
wiring.not_changed: no explicit `index` prop was added to the shipped thumb. A single thumb resolves to 0 on its own and pinning it would change the generated ids controls.test.tsx renders against, for no benefit.

wiring.added: documentation only — a section stating why the catalogue does not appear in this file
wiring.reason: all three of its engine strings (roleDescription, incrementLabel, decrementLabel) are already REQUIRED PROPS on Lumo's frozen public API. The catalogue's precedence rule is `explicit prop, else catalogue`; a required prop is always explicit, so the catalogue can never fire. Routing them through it would mean relaxing three required props to optional — an API change this experiment may not make and a house rule it may not weaken.
wiring.not_wasted: the catalogue is still where their values come from — the call site reads stringsFor(locale).numberField.*, and base-ui-strings.ts imports roleDescription from that same entry so the two catalogues cannot drift into two Persian phrases for one concept.

coverage.$rule: one row per reachable string. `closed_by` is what actually puts the Persian in the served bytes TODAY, not what could.

tally.$read_this_row_not_the_headline: The layer's value today is not a violation count going down — the two shipped Base UI components that leak were already closed by props. Its value is that seven strings now have ONE typed source that resolves on the server, that a compile error appears when a locale is added, and that a suite fails when Base UI moves a literal. Claiming seven newly-fixed strings would be false.

the_suite.why_a_permanent_test_and_not_a_probe: probe.base-ui-i18n.mjs measured that seven of eight strings are prop-reachable. A measurement is true on the day it is taken. All seven reach through mergeProps precedence and `?? default` fallbacks — internal choices with no compatibility promise. A minor that moves one literal after the spread turns a Persian page English with a green build, no type error and no visible change. This is patch.test.tsx's job on the Base UI side.
the_suite.why_the_negative_assertion_is_the_load_b: each case asserts the Persian string is PRESENT and the English string Base UI would otherwise emit is ABSENT. Asserting only presence passes on a page carrying both values on the same attribute, which is not hypothetical — strings.ts records React Aria's NumberField <Group> doing exactly that.
the_suite.why_english_has_its_own_arm: if en-US fell through to Base UI's own defaults rather than resolving through the catalogue, a wiring regression would appear in one locale only and the other would keep passing. The English arm takes the same code path on purpose.
the_suite.bare_carrier_cases_are_labelled_as_such: Progress.Root, Toast.Viewport and the two-thumb Slider are rendered directly because no Base UI-engine Lumo component exists for them. That proves the catalogue reaches the attribute; it does not prove a Lumo component threads it, and the file says so at each case.

measured_outputs.numberfield_fa_IR: aria-roledescription="فیلد عددی", aria-label="افزایش تعداد", aria-label="کاهش تعداد"; zero occurrences of "Number field", "Increase", "Decrease"
measured_outputs.progress_indeterminate_fa_IR: aria-valuetext="پیشرفت نامعین"; zero occurrences of "indeterminate progress"
measured_outputs.slider_range_fa_IR: aria-valuetext="۲۰ آغاز بازه" and aria-valuetext="۶۰ پایان بازه"; zero occurrences of "start range"/"end range"

the_suite.the_assertion_that_would_have_been_vacuo: "contains a Persian character" alone. «۲۰ start range» satisfies it. Each fa-IR static entry is additionally asserted NOT to match /[A-Za-z]{3,}/, which is the half-translated shape the census called the hardest of the eight to notice.

four_independent_reasons: line 14: `function ComboboxInternalDismissButton(_, forwardedRef)` — the props argument is discarded at the signature, so there is no object to override into
the literal sits AFTER `...dismissProps` (line 31), so even a props path would lose to it
not importable: 83 export subpaths, none resolving into combobox/utils/; its .d.ts is `export {};`
constructed by its parents — ComboboxInput.mjs:368 and ComboboxPopup.mjs:115 — neither of which forwards consumer props to it
the_unreachable_one.no_node_modules_reach_attempted: confirmed by READING the dist, which is what the brief permits. Nothing imports from an internal module path and no file under node_modules was modified. The gap is recorded as not externally fixable, which is the finding.
the_unreachable_one.draft_is_a_comment_not_a_new_issue: mui/base-ui#5263 is open and a core maintainer (atomiks) already accepted 'a prop can work in the meantime'. A duplicate issue would cost triage time and buy nothing. What the thread lacks is a concrete prop shape and a 1.7.0 confirmation; the draft supplies both.
the_unreachable_one.proposed_api: `labels?: { dismiss?: string }` on Combobox.Root, threaded onto the store the sentinel ALREADY subscribes to (it imports and calls useComboboxRootContext on lines 9 and 15), read as `store.state.labels?.dismiss ?? 'Dismiss'`. An object rather than a flat `dismissLabel` so the promised translations provider has a shape to merge into with ordinary precedence and no deprecation.
the_unreachable_one.maintainer_objection_addressed_not_dodge: atomiks's concern is that a niche prop is easy to miss. The draft concedes it: a prop nobody sets leaves today's English in place, which is no worse than today. What it buys is that the string stops being unreachable. A dev-only warning is explicitly NOT proposed — it would fire on every English application, and a warning everybody silences is worse than none.

the_unreported_one.claim: every control Base UI names through Field.Label renders on the server with no accessible name at all
the_unreported_one.framed_as: a WCAG 4.1.2 bug in the served bytes — not a feature request

prior_art_search.method: GitHub search API over repo:mui/base-ui, two queries
prior_art_search.result: no open or closed issue reports it
prior_art_search.nearest_neighbour: #4142, merged 2026-02-24, '[checkbox][switch][radio] Add automatic aria-labelledby support' — the PR that INTRODUCED the mechanism

cause.route_1: utils/useRegisteredLabelId.js — `setLabelId(id)` is the only write and it is inside useIsoLayoutEffect
cause.route_2: internals/labelable-provider/useAriaLabelledBy.js — the DOM-scanning fallback is inside useIsoLayoutEffect too, and it MUTATES the DOM (`label.id = generatedLabelId`), so it can only ever be client-side as written
cause.consequence: on the server both are undefined, and line 9's `explicitAriaLabelledBy ?? labelId ?? fallbackAriaLabelledBy` yields undefined

repro_measured_first_hand_2026_08_11.a_detail_worth_more_than_the_headline: the served <label for> targets the aria-hidden="true" PROXY INPUT. The association exists and resolves to an element removed from the accessibility tree, so the label names nothing a screen reader can reach. That is a second, independent defect and the draft asks for it too.
repro_measured_first_hand_2026_08_11.why_a_wrapping_label_does_not_save_it: a native <label> names only labelable ELEMENTS. A <span> carrying a role is not one; the only labelable element inside is the aria-hidden proxy. This is what makes the defect Base-UI-specific rather than a general SSR caveat — a library exposing a real <input> is named by the platform with no JavaScript at all.

the_unreported_one.why_nobody_has_noticed: it SELF-HEALS on hydration, so every test tier except a served-bytes tier is green. jsdom, Testing Library, getByRole({name}), axe-in-a-browser — all observe the post-hydration DOM and all pass.
the_unreported_one.proposed_fix: resolve aria-labelledby during render: mint the label id in Field.Root (the common ancestor, which already renders before both) and put it on the context value; emit aria-labelledby on the control from that value; keep useRegisteredLabelId's effect as the reconciliation path for labels that mount, unmount or change id later, but stop it being the only source of the first byte. Point Field.Label's `for` at the exposed control or drop it. The DOM-scanning fallback may stay an effect — there is no DOM to scan on the server.
the_unreported_one.why_the_fix_is_credible: line 9 already consults `explicitAriaLabelledBy` FIRST and synchronously, ahead of both effects. The render-time naming path exists; only the id is missing.

limitations: NO GATE RUN. Per the brief, no `pnpm run verify` and no `next build`. So there is no new gate:html number here — the 98/12 figures are quoted from phase-a-result.json, not re-measured.

TWO OF THE SEVEN ARE ASSERTED ON BARE CARRIERS, NOT ON LUMO COMPONENTS. progress.tsx and toast.tsx are still React Aria. The suite proves the catalogue reaches Progress.Root's and Toast.Viewport's attributes; it does not prove a future Lumo wrapper will thread them, because that wrapper does not exist.

THE SLIDER RANGE BRANCH IS NOT EXERCISED BY THE SHIPPED COMPONENT. Lumo ships one thumb. The branch is covered by a bare-carrier render and by catalogue unit tests, not by rendering Lumo's Slider with two thumbs — which is impossible without changing its public API, since SliderProps is typed AriaSliderProps<number>.
NOTHING WAS RENDERED IN A BROWSER. Every claim here is about served bytes and jsdom, the same limitation phase-a-result.json records.

THE UPSTREAM DRAFTS ARE DRAFTS. Neither has been filed. Issue and PR metadata was read via the GitHub API on 2026-08-11 and is quoted with its measured state; the maintainer quote on #5263 was already captured in base-ui-upstream-policy.json and is re-quoted, not re-interpreted.

CONCURRENT WORKTREE. A sibling agent is editing base-ui-adapter.ts, checkbox.tsx and switch.tsx in the same checkout during this run. The 8 pre-existing tsc errors come from that work; none are in the files this brief touched, and none were repaired, because repairing another agent's in-flight file would collide.
